title: incident-bot: prioritize SLO-linked runbook suggestions and enrich telemetry context for on-call diagnostics
author: Asha Patel
description: Motivation: On recent on-call rotations we observed runbook suggestions returned by incident-bot that were not closely correlated with active SLO breaches. Engineers had to manually triage noisy suggestions while investigating urgent alerts. This PR improves the relevance of runbook suggestions for on-call workflows by prioritizing runbooks that are linked to SLOs associated with the incident signal and by enriching telemetry context so suggested runbooks show a small snapshot of related metrics.
changes_summary:
- Add SLO-aware ranking heuristic that boosts runbooks linked to SLOs when the incident matches the SLO's service scope.
- Enrich diagnostics context payload with precomputed metric snapshots and recent breach history to display inline in Slack/Console suggestions.
- Add lightweight matching layer that ties alert tags (service/component) to SLO metadata via the slo-toolkit index.
- Unit + integration tests for ranking and telemetry enrichment; e2e test for Slack suggestion flow.
- Docs: update runbook suggestion behaviour in oncall-playbook.md

release_notes: Improved incident-bot runbook suggestions: SLO-linked runbooks are prioritized when the incident signal matches SLO service metadata; suggestions now include a small telemetry snapshot and recent SLO breach history to help on-call triage.
post_deploy_notes: Rolled out to staging 2025-11-10, smoke-tested on a synthetic alert. Gradual rollout to production over 2 hours; monitoring for suggestion latency and suggestion relevance metrics (incidents with on-call ack within 15m).
tests_and_validation:

- Integration test validates ranking preference for SLO-linked runbooks.
- E2E Slack flow validated against staging channel (#oncall-staging).
- Observability: added histogram for suggestion latency and gauge for % of incidents with SLO-linked suggestion at top position.
notes: Design tradeoffs: We intentionally keep ranking weights conservative (small boost) to avoid hiding non-SLO runbooks that are still relevant. Index lookups are cached for 30s to avoid extra latency in hot paths. If an SLO's metadata is unavailable we fall back to current keyword matching behavior.
